title: Hidden Thread
description: Five source-backed questions, then a connection to find in your own words. Optional clues and choices are available.

threads.title: Five different worlds
threads.teaser: An instrument, two words, a computer test, and a fictional spy. Find the connection after all five.
choices: Each borrowed its name from a real person
Each borrowed its name from a real place
Each borrowed its name from another language's word for a sound
Each was named after a fictional character
threads.connection: The saxophone, boycott, silhouette, Turing test, and James Bond each take a name from a real person.

links.summary: Saxophone: its inventor’s surname was Sax.
links.explanation: The saxophone carries instrument maker Adolphe Sax’s surname.

links.summary: Charles Boycott: a land agent isolated during an Irish rent dispute.
links.explanation: The word boycott grew from the organized isolation of land agent Charles Boycott.

links.summary: Étienne de Silhouette: a French finance minister.
links.explanation: The word silhouette preserves the surname of French finance minister Étienne de Silhouette.

links.summary: CAPTCHA: its T stands for Turing test.
links.explanation: CAPTCHA refers to the Turing test, named after Alan Turing.

links.summary: James Bond: the reference book on Fleming’s shelf covered Caribbean birds.
links.explanation: Ian Fleming borrowed the name James Bond from the ornithologist who wrote Birds of the West Indies.

threads.hint: Think about how each subject got its name.
